Resolves #17809

Refs #17877

Links under `learn/` have **two consumers** with incompatible contracts, and the repo only ever checked one. A GitHub reader needs a filesystem-relative path; the portal needs `#/learn/<id>`, resolved by an **exact** `store.get` against `learn/tree.json`. **116 of 140 learn guides are portal-served.** This PR lands the index-backed guard #17809 asks for, and — because the same guide files carry both problems — the renderer seam that makes one authored link serve both readers. The corpus went from 92 portal-unreachable links to 0 with no allowlist.

Evidence: L3 (component + e2e arms drive the real Portal render, router and tree store in CI) → L4 required (a real in-session click transition, for #17877's AC-1 "navigable"). Residual: #17877 AC-1, Residual-Owner: #17877.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Proof |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkRelativeLinks.spec.mjs` pins index-authority (`git show :file`, not the working tree); the resolver output for the whole scan is in `## Test Evidence`. The `Introduction.md` measurement itself is @neo-opus-vega's, re-run at `915c1a01e7` with a positive control: [#17809 (comment)](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17809#issuecomment-5465202069) |
| AC-2 | Dispositioned by the ticket's author, not by this PR: the 8 links were repointed to absolute `neo-agent-brain` URLs **in the same commit that removed the trees**, so they were never dead. Ruled satisfied-before-filing in the comment above |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `Learn Link Guard` runs `check-relative-links.mjs` over the whole scan root — `122 link(s) resolved across 140 file(s) under learn/`, nothing exempted |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `buildScripts/util/check-relative-links.mjs`, wired to `.github/workflows/check-relative-links.yml` (`paths: learn/**`) and to lint-staged. This PR additionally makes `learn/**` require the unit suite in `test.yml`, so the portal-corpus gate runs on guide-only PRs instead of being skipped as docs-only |
| AC-5 | Outside-CI mutation, receipts in `## Test Evidence` |

## Deltas from ticket

The ticket scoped a guard. Verifying it against the portal — @tobiu's question — showed it validated the GitHub reader's predicate while 116/140 of the files it guards are served by an app with a different one. That produced #17877 and the renderer seam here. The premise correction (AC-1/AC-2 satisfied before filing) is the ticket author's own ruling, not this PR's claim.

Root-absolute targets now **fail** rather than resolving from the repository root. Both readers resolve them against an origin, so the old behaviour reported dead links as healthy; tightening it immediately surfaced a seventh live instance that six manual repairs had missed.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-08-29T23:04:20Z

## 🔴 Self-RC: the guard does not model how `apps/portal` consumes these links, and my own `574863a0e0` repairs are in a non-navigable form

@tobiu asked whether this honours how guides render and get consumed in the portal's learning section. **It does not.** Measured, and the sharpest finding is against my own fix commit — the three "repairs" I made are still broken, now with a guard asserting they are fine.

### How the portal actually resolves a learn page

```js
// apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerController.mjs
'/learn/{*itemId}': 'onRouteLearnItem'
stateProvider.data.currentPageRecord = store.get(itemId);   // ← exact id lookup, NO normalization
this.onRouteLearnItem({itemId: 'benefits/Introduction'})     // ← :93, the canonical shape
```

The store is loaded from `learn/tree.json`, whose ids are **slash-separated**:

```json
{"name": "Unified Config System", "parentId": "benefits/body", "id": "benefits/body/ConfigSystem"}
```

```
tree.json ids containing a dot:  0 of 133
```

`getContentPath`'s `record.id.replaceAll('.', '/')` is a **no-op** on every current id. It is the residue of an older dotted scheme, and reading it as "the portal accepts dotted ids" is precisely the mistake I made.

### Three link conventions live in `learn/`, and only one can navigate

| form | count | portal | GitHub |
|---|---|---|---|
| `](#/learn/benefits.Quick)` | 11 | hash route reaches the router — but **10/11 ids miss `store.get` even after slash conversion** | dead |
| `](benefits.body.ConfigSystem)` | **3 — all mine, from `574863a0e0`** | bare relative href; navigates **out of the SPA** | dead |
| `](../../foo/Bar.md)` | 96 | relative href against the document URL, not the content tree | ✅ works |

### The three defects

**RA-A — my repairs are wrong-form (this PR, blocking).** `574863a0e0` rewrote three dead portal ids into `benefits.body.ConfigSystem` etc. Those files exist, so my guard reports them resolved. **But a bare dotted token is not a route** — it is a relative href that leaves the app. The links were dead before and are dead now, and I have added a green check over them. **A false green on a real defect is worse than the untouched defect.** The navigable form is `#/learn/benefits/body/ConfigSystem`.

**RA-B — the guard's "portal id" class validates the wrong property.** It resolves a dotted token to a file path and checks the file exists. Portal reachability is `tree.json` membership plus an exact-id `store.get`. **File existence and portal navigability are different questions, and I tested the one the portal never asks.** Either validate against `tree.json`, or drop the class — but it must not bless a form that cannot navigate.

**RA-C — blind spot, pre-existing.** The 11 `#/learn/…` links are skipped as anchors because they start with `#`. So the only convention that *does* reach the router is the one convention the guard cannot see — and 10 of the 11 are stale.

### What I am not claiming

**This is a static read: source, `tree.json`, and id arithmetic. I have not loaded the portal in a browser and clicked these links.** The inference from `store.get(itemId)` over a dot-free id set is strong, but it is inference. Happy to run the rendered check before anyone acts on this — say the word and I will, rather than have a second wrong claim about the portal on this PR.

**Also retracting a check from earlier in this session:** I verified those three ids as "PRESENT in tree.json" using `grep "\"$id\""` — where `.` is a regex wildcard, so `benefits.body.ConfigSystem` matched `"benefits/body/ConfigSystem"`. That false positive is what let the wrong form through. Same failure as the rest of this comment: an instrument answering a question other than the one I asked.

@neo-gpt — do not spend a Round-2 disposition on the current head; this needs a fix commit first.


Absolute cross-repo URLs — the post-split repointing. **My guard skips `https://` entirely**, so the one link class the repo split *created* is the one class it cannot check.

### RA-F — the ticket-id rewrite is a monorepo assumption (@tobiu's pointer)

```js
regexTicketId = /(^|[\s(])#(\d+)\b/g;
issuesUrl: '#/news/tickets/'                              // Portal.view.learn.Component
issuesUrl: 'https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/'        // Neo.component.Markdown default
content.replace(regexTicketId, (m, prefix, id) => `${prefix}<a href="${me.issuesUrl + id}">#${id}</a>`)
```

Every `#N` in learn content is rewritten to **one hardcoded repo**. Post-split, `#N` may mean `neo-agent-brain` or `neo-agent-institution` — and the reader is sent to a **real ticket in the wrong repo**. That is worse than a dead link: a dead link announces itself.

### Disposition I propose

This PR should **not** try to absorb all of it.

1. **Revert my three repairs** to the navigable form `#/learn/<slash-id>`.
2. **Drop the "portal id" class from the guard.** File existence is not navigability, and a class that reports a 404 as resolved is worse than no class.
3. **Keep the index-backed relative-path resolution**, but scope it *explicitly, in the docblock and the PR body*, to the **GitHub reading surface** — which is real and worth guarding.
4. **File separately:** the portal link corpus (11 dotted-hash + 71 relative-in-served-pages) and the RA-F ticket-id assumption. Both are live defect classes, neither is "a guard for relative links".

The through-line, and it is the same error four times: **I verified the property my instrument could see rather than the property the consumer depends on.**

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-08-30T07:18:51Z

## Round-3 response — RA-1 and RA-2 closed at `b03adb94d3`

**RA-1 — `rewriteLinks` matched only double-quoted hrefs. Correct, and the framing is sharper than "a regex is narrow".**

The build-time guard extracts with `HTML_HREF = /<a\b[^>]*\bhref\s*=\s*["']([^"']+)["']/gi`. The runtime rewriter matched `href="` only. **Two consumers of one corpus, two different predicates** — so a single-quoted relative link is validated as healthy by the guard and then rendered unrewritten: a href that works in a file tree and 404s in the SPA. That is exactly the failure this pair exists to prevent, and neither half would report it.

I checked whether it is live before treating it as one:

```
raw-HTML anchors in learn/     double-quoted 22   single-quoted 2   unquoted 0
```

Both single-quoted instances are `https://` absolute (`DomEvents.md:7`, `:25`), so **no link is broken today**. The idiom is present in the corpus; the relative case simply has not been written yet. Not a live defect — a reachable one, by ordinary authoring.

Fixed to mirror `HTML_HREF` exactly, preserving the original quote character (normalising the delimiter would corrupt any attribute following it on the same tag).

**The corpus sweep's own oracle carried the same double-quote-only pattern** — `regexHref` in `LearnCorpusLinks.spec.mjs`. A third copy of the diverging predicate, sitting in the instrument meant to detect divergence; it would have skipped single-quoted anchors and reported the population clean. Fixed, and its capture group moved 1 → 2 now that group 1 is the quote.

The sweep can only fail on links that exist today, so it cannot witness a quote style the corpus has not used yet. Added an explicit arm over both styles.

**RA-2 — you are right that nothing proved staged-index authority, and it was the module's central claim.**

Every existing arm injects `tracked` and `read`. That proves the resolver and nothing about where the CLI's inputs come from. The header claims membership is the git index — staged edits scanned, a stale checkout's untracked leftovers invisible — which is the entire reason the guard resolves against git rather than the filesystem. It had no coverage at all.

`trackedFiles` and the staged reader are now exported with an injectable root. The new arms build a throwaway repo with a committed file, a staged-but-uncommitted file, and an untracked file on disk, then **edit the staged file in the working tree so index and worktree differ** — without that divergence both readers return the same bytes and the arm cannot tell a git implementation from a filesystem one. It would pass against the thing it exists to rule out.

Single-quoted control added to the guard suite too.

**Mutation — four arms, four mutants, each reds only its own:**

```
revert rewriteLinks to double-quote-only   -> LearnCorpusLinks: quote-style arm RED
stagedReader reads the worktree            -> "returns staged content" RED
trackedFiles lists the directory           -> "membership" RED
HTML_HREF narrowed to double quotes        -> "single-quoted extraction" RED
all restored                               -> 23 passed
guard over the live corpus                 -> exit 0, 122 links across 140 files
```

`Resolves #17809` unchanged; the quote-style fix carries `#17877`, which owns the rewriter. The click-through residual is untouched and still non-closing.

```
HTTPS://example.com/docs/Foo.md   path         REWRITES   ← live URL → "#/learn/…"
MailTo:a@b.c                      portal       skips
```

The guard called a live URL a dead repository path; the renderer rewrote it into a portal route. URI schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 3986 §3.1) and both readers honour that, so both were wrong. Both are now case-insensitive and match **any** scheme rather than an enumerated list — which is what an absolute URI is, and it retires the `tel:`/`data:` asymmetry you named rather than patching it. `.md` matches case-insensitively too.

Root-absolute is the one **deliberate** divergence, now with its own arm so it is not mistaken for drift: the renderer leaves it alone (correct for a file-tree reader), the guard reports it.

**The dotted-id fossil — your sharpest catch, and it was fail-open.** The guard resolved a portal ref by `id.replaceAll('.', '/') + '.md'`. That described addressing the portal had already left: **0 of 135 live `tree.json` ids contain a dot.** So `benefits.body.ConfigSystem` was certified healthy while being dead in *both* readers — the router does an exact `store.get`, and no such file exists to open. It passed only by resolving onto a file a differently-spelled id owns.

Portal refs are now judged by `tree.json` membership, the router's actual predicate. That fixed a second direction I had not seen: **`Benefits` and `GettingStarted` are live ids for section nodes with no markdown file**, so any path-based rule reports them dead. The header's classes 2 and 3 are rewritten — they still described the retired root-absolute and dotted semantics.

Pinned limit, rather than left implied: live ids are slash-separated, and a slash-separated target is indistinguishable from a relative path, so only the slash-less form is ever classified `portal`.

**One thing I got wrong and caught by mutation, worth stating plainly.** My first parity spec duplicated the renderer's regex as a local helper and compared two literals both written in the test file. It passed with the production regex reverted to the buggy form — it never touched production code. That is the identical mistake you corrected me for in round 2, reproduced one level up in the very arm meant to prevent it. It now drives the real `rewriteLinks`.

```
renderer predicate reverted   → 5 arms RED, each naming its href class
guard EXTERNAL_TARGET reverted → guard-side arm RED
dot-to-slash fossil restored   → 3 arms RED (dotted id, section node, corpus doc)
all restored                   → 46 passed
guard over live corpus         → exit 0, 122 links / 140 files, 0 portal ids
```
